questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.prompt: Paint Like a Beast students blended edges smoothly

block.label: Swipe Sort
block.sub: Flick each card up into its bucket

questions.why: False — the project favoured loose, energetic brushwork over smooth blending, since the goal was texture and movement, not a soft, careful finish.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A daimyo controlled land on behalf of the shogun

block.label: Swipe Sort
block.sub: Flick each card up into its bucket

questions.why: True — daimyo were regional lords who governed land granted by the shogun, in exchange for loyalty and military support.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What title does Prince Escalus hold over Verona?
questions.why: Escalus is called 'Prince' of Verona, the ruler who tries to keep peace between the feuding families; students sometimes assume a bigger title like King since he has supreme authority.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In C–Am–F–G, which chord plays the dominant 'V' role?
questions.why: G is the 'V' chord, creating tension that pulls strongly back to the tonic C. Students often mix it up with F (the 'IV'), which supports rather than pulls.

questions.subject: Visual Arts
questions.prompt: What did Paint Like a Beast students mostly use to apply paint, besides brushes?
questions.why: Sponges and rags were used alongside brushes to build texture and loose marks; rulers and tape would create the precise, controlled edges the project deliberately avoided.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these events in a feudal land grant, from what happens first to what happens last
questions.why: A daimyo first pledged loyalty to the shogun, who then granted land in return; the daimyo collected rice tax from that land and used it to pay the samurai who served him.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these questions a historian asks about change, from the shortest timescale to the longest
sequence: What stayed the same for centuries?
questions.why: Historians weigh change across different timescales, from a single year up to centuries, to judge whether something was a quick shift or a deep continuity.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: What does Juliet ask Romeo to send word of, the day after the party?
questions.why: Juliet tells the Nurse to find Romeo and ask if he intends marriage; if so, she'll send word of a time and place. Students sometimes forget how fast the plot moves — marriage is arranged within a day of meeting.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which theatre in London was strongly associated with Shakespeare's plays?
questions.why: The Globe Theatre was where Shakespeare's company performed most of his plays; students sometimes confuse it with The Rose, an earlier, separate Elizabethan playhouse.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: Explain why starting the same four chords, C-Am-F-G, on Am instead of C can make a song feel sadder, even though the chords used are identical.
